# base64 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base64/^0.22.1/

## Expand description

Correct, fast, and configurable [base64](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Base64) decoding and encoding. Base64
transports binary data efficiently in contexts where only plain text is
allowed.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Use an [ Engine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html) to decode or encode base64, configured with the base64
alphabet and padding behavior best suited to your application.

[§](https://docs.rs#engine-setup)Engine setup

There is more than one way to encode a stream of bytes as “base64”.
Different applications use different encoding
[alphabets](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html) and
[padding behaviors](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurposeConfig.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#encoding-alphabet)Encoding alphabet

Almost all base64 [alphabets](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html) use `A-Z`, `a-z`, and
`0-9`, which gives nearly 64 characters (26 + 26 + 10 = 62), but they differ
in their choice of their final 2.

Most applications use the [standard](https://docs.rs/alphabet/constant.STANDARD.html) alphabet specified
in [RFC 4648](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4648#section-4).  If that’s all you need, you can get started
quickly by using the pre-configured
[ STANDARD](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/constant.STANDARD.html) engine, which is also available
in the

[module as shown here, if you prefer a minimal](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)

`prelude``use`
footprint.```
use base64::prelude::*;
assert_eq!(BASE64_STANDARD.decode(b"+uwgVQA=")?, b"\xFA\xEC\x20\x55\0");
assert_eq!(BASE64_STANDARD.encode(b"\xFF\xEC\x20\x55\0"), "/+wgVQA=");
```
Other common alphabets are available in the [ alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/index.html) module.

[§](https://docs.rs#url-safe-alphabet)URL-safe alphabet

The standard alphabet uses `+` and `/` as its two non-alphanumeric tokens,
which cannot be safely used in URL’s without encoding them as `%2B` and
`%2F`.

To avoid that, some applications use a [“URL-safe” alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/constant.URL_SAFE.html),
which uses `-` and `_` instead. To use that alternative alphabet, use the
[ URL_SAFE](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/constant.URL_SAFE.html) engine. This example doesn’t
use

[to show what a more explicit](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)

`prelude``use` would look like.```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE, Engine as _};
assert_eq!(URL_SAFE.decode(b"-uwgVQA=")?, b"\xFA\xEC\x20\x55\0");
assert_eq!(URL_SAFE.encode(b"\xFF\xEC\x20\x55\0"), "_-wgVQA=");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#padding-characters)Padding characters

Each base64 character represents 6 bits (2⁶ = 64) of the original binary data, and every 3 bytes of input binary data will encode to 4 base64 characters (8 bits × 3 = 6 bits × 4 = 24 bits).

When the input is not an even multiple of 3 bytes in length, [canonical](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4648#section-3.5)
base64 encoders insert padding characters at the end, so that the output
length is always a multiple of 4:

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, Engine as _};
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b""),    "");
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b"f"),   "Zg==");
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b"fo"),  "Zm8=");
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b"foo"), "Zm9v");
```
Canonical encoding ensures that base64 encodings will be exactly the same,
byte-for-byte, regardless of input length. But the `=` padding characters
aren’t necessary for decoding, and they may be omitted by using a
[ NO_PAD](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/constant.NO_PAD.html) configuration:

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD_NO_PAD, Engine as _};
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b""),    "");
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b"f"),   "Zg");
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b"fo"),  "Zm8");
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b"foo"), "Zm9v");
```
The pre-configured `NO_PAD` engines will reject inputs containing padding
`=` characters. To encode without padding and still accept padding while
decoding, create an [engine](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurpose.html) with
that [padding mode](https://docs.rs/engine/enum.DecodePaddingMode.html).

`assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.decode(b"Zm8="), Err(base64::DecodeError::InvalidPadding));`[§](https://docs.rs#further-customization)Further customization

Decoding and encoding behavior can be customized by creating an
[engine](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurpose.html) with an [alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html) and
[padding configuration](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurposeConfig.html):

```
use base64::{engine, alphabet, Engine as _};
// bizarro-world base64: +/ as the first symbols instead of the last
let alphabet =
    alphabet::Alphabet::new("+/ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789")
    .unwrap();
// a very weird config that encodes with padding but requires no padding when decoding...?
let crazy_config = engine::GeneralPurposeConfig::new()
    .with_decode_allow_trailing_bits(true)
    .with_encode_padding(true)
    .with_decode_padding_mode(engine::DecodePaddingMode::RequireNone);
let crazy_engine = engine::GeneralPurpose::new(&alphabet, crazy_config);
let encoded = crazy_engine.encode(b"abc 123");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#memory-allocation)Memory allocation

The [decode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.decode) and [encode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.encode) engine methods
allocate memory for their results – `decode` returns a `Vec<u8>` and
`encode` returns a `String`. To instead decode or encode into a buffer that
you allocated, use one of the alternative methods:

[§](https://docs.rs#decoding)Decoding

| Method | Output | Allocates memory |
|---|---|---|
| `Engine::decode` | returns a new `Vec<u8>` | always |
| `Engine::decode_vec` | appends to provided `Vec<u8>` | if `Vec`lacks capacity |
| `Engine::decode_slice` | writes to provided `&[u8]` | never |

[§](https://docs.rs#encoding)Encoding

| Method | Output | Allocates memory |
|---|---|---|
| `Engine::encode` | returns a new `String` | always |
| `Engine::encode_string` | appends to provided `String` | if `String`lacks capacity |
| `Engine::encode_slice` | writes to provided `&[u8]` | never |

[§](https://docs.rs#input-and-output)Input and output

The `base64` crate can [decode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.decode) and
[encode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.encode) values in memory, or
[ DecoderReader](https://docs.rs/read/struct.DecoderReader.html) and

[provide streaming decoding and encoding for any](https://docs.rs/write/struct.EncoderWriter.html)

`EncoderWriter`[readable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html)or

[writable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Write.html)byte stream.

[§](https://docs.rs#decoding-1)Decoding

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, read::DecoderReader};
let mut input = io::stdin();
let mut decoder = DecoderReader::new(&mut input, &STANDARD);
io::copy(&mut decoder, &mut io::stdout())?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#encoding-1)Encoding

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, write::EncoderWriter};
let mut output = io::stdout();
let mut encoder = EncoderWriter::new(&mut output, &STANDARD);
io::copy(&mut io::stdin(), &mut encoder)?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#display)Display

If you only need a base64 representation for implementing the
[ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) trait, use

[:](https://docs.rs/display/struct.Base64Display.html)

`Base64Display````
use base64::{display::Base64Display, engine::general_purpose::STANDARD};
let value = Base64Display::new(b"\0\x01\x02\x03", &STANDARD);
assert_eq!("base64: AAECAw==", format!("base64: {}", value));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

If length calculations result in overflowing `usize`, a panic will result.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use engine::`- [Engine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/index.html)
- Provides [Alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html)and constants for alphabets commonly used in the wild.
- [display](https://docs.rs/display/index.html)
- Enables base64’d output anywhere you might use a `Display`implementation, like a format string.
- [engine](https://docs.rs/engine/index.html)
- Provides the [Engine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html)abstraction and out of the box implementations.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Preconfigured engines for common use cases.
- [read](https://docs.rs/read/index.html)
- Implementations of `io::Read`to transparently decode base64.
- [write](https://docs.rs/write/index.html)
- Implementations of `io::Write`to transparently handle base64.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeError.html)- Error
- Errors that can occur while decoding.
- [Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeSliceError.html)- Slice - Error
- Errors that can occur while decoding into a slice.
- [Encode](https://docs.rs/enum.EncodeSliceError.html)- Slice - Error
- Errors that can occur while encoding into a slice.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode](https://docs.rs/fn.decode.html)- Deprecated
- Decode base64 using the `STANDARD`engine
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_engine.html)- engine - Deprecated
- Decode from string reference as octets using the specified [Engine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html).
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_engine_slice.html)- engine_ - slice - Deprecated
- Decode the input into the provided output slice.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_engine_vec.html)- engine_ - vec - Deprecated
- Decode from string reference as octets.
- [decoded_](https://docs.rs/fn.decoded_len_estimate.html)- len_ - estimate
- Returns a conservative estimate of the decoded size of `encoded_len`base64 symbols (rounded up to the next group of 3 decoded bytes).
- [encode](https://docs.rs/fn.encode.html)- Deprecated
- Encode arbitrary octets as base64 using the `STANDARD`engine
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_engine.html)- engine - Deprecated
- Encode arbitrary octets as base64 using the provided `Engine`into a new`String`.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_engine_slice.html)- engine_ - slice - Deprecated
- Encode arbitrary octets as base64 into a supplied slice.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_engine_string.html)- engine_ - string - Deprecated
- Encode arbitrary octets as base64 into a supplied `String`.
- [encoded_](https://docs.rs/fn.encoded_len.html)- len
- Calculate the base64 encoded length for a given input length, optionally including any appropriate padding bytes.

# pico_args - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pico-args/^0.5/

## Expand description

An ultra simple CLI arguments parser.

If you think that this library doesn’t support some feature, it’s probably intentional.

- No help generation
- Only flags, options, free arguments and subcommands are supported
- No combined flags (like `-vvv`or`-abc`)
- Options can be separated by a space, `=`or nothing. See build features
- Arguments can be in any order
- Non UTF-8 arguments are supported

[§](https://docs.rs#build-features)Build features

-
`eq-separator`Allows parsing arguments separated by `=`
 This feature adds about 1KiB to the resulting binary
-
`short-space-opt`Makes the space between short keys and their values optional (e.g. `-w10`)
 If`eq-separator`is enabled, then it takes precedence and the ‘=’ is not included.
 If`eq-separator`is disabled, then`-K=value`gives an error instead of returning`"=value"`.
 The optional space is only applicable for short keys because`--keyvalue`would be ambiguous
-
`combined-flags`Allows combination of flags, e.g.`-abc`instead of`-a -b -c`.
 If`short-space-opt`or`eq-separator`are enabled, you must parse flags after values, to prevent ambiguities.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Arguments](https://docs.rs/struct.Arguments.html)
- An arguments parser.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- A list of possible errors.

# tiny_skia_path - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tiny-skia-path/^0.11.4/

## Expand description

A [tiny-skia](https://github.com/RazrFalcon/tiny-skia) Bezier path implementation.

Provides a memory-efficient Bezier path container, path builder, path stroker and path dasher.

Also provides some basic geometry types, but they will be moved to an external crate eventually.

Note that all types use single precision floats (`f32`), just like [Skia](https://skia.org/).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [path_](https://docs.rs/path_geometry/index.html)- geometry
- A collection of functions to work with Bezier paths.

# xmlwriter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xmlwriter/^0.1/

## Expand description

A simple, streaming, partially-validating XML writer that writes XML data into an internal buffer.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- A simple, bare-minimum, panic-based API.
- Non-allocating API. All methods are accepting either `fmt::Display`or`fmt::Arguments`.
- Nodes auto-closing.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use xmlwriter::*;
let opt = Options {
    use_single_quote: true,
    ..Options::default()
};
let mut w = XmlWriter::new(opt);
w.start_element("svg");
w.write_attribute("xmlns", "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg");
w.write_attribute_fmt("viewBox", format_args!("{} {} {} {}", 0, 0, 128, 128));
w.start_element("text");
// We can write any object that implements `fmt::Display`.
w.write_attribute("x", &10);
w.write_attribute("y", &20);
w.write_text_fmt(format_args!("length is {}", 5));
assert_eq!(w.end_document(),
"<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 128 128'>
    <text x='10' y='20'>
        length is 5
    </text>
</svg>
");
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Indent](https://docs.rs/enum.Indent.html)
- An XML node indention.

# ttf_parser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ttf-parser/latest/target-redirect/ttf_parser/

## Expand description

A high-level, safe, zero-allocation font parser for:

Font parsing starts with a [ Face](https://docs.rs/struct.Face.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- A high-level API for most common properties, hiding all parsing and data resolving logic.
- A low-level, but safe API to access TrueType tables data.
- Highly configurable. You can disable most of the features, reducing binary size. You can also parse TrueType tables separately, without loading the whole font/face.
- Zero heap allocations.
- Zero unsafe.
- Zero dependencies.
- `no_std`/WASM compatible.
- Fast.
- Stateless. All parsing methods are immutable.
- Simple and maintainable code (no magic numbers).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- The library must not panic. Any panic considered as a critical bug and should be reported.
- The library forbids unsafe code.
- No heap allocations, so crash due to OOM is not possible.
- All recursive methods have a depth limit.
- Technically, should use less than 64KiB of stack in worst case scenario.
- Most of arithmetic operations are checked.
- Most of numeric casts are checked.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

# ttf_parser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ttf-parser/0.21.1/target-redirect/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/ttf_parser/

## Expand description

A high-level, safe, zero-allocation font parser for:

Font parsing starts with a [ Face](https://docs.rs/struct.Face.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- A high-level API for most common properties, hiding all parsing and data resolving logic.
- A low-level, but safe API to access TrueType tables data.
- Highly configurable. You can disable most of the features, reducing binary size. You can also parse TrueType tables separately, without loading the whole font/face.
- Zero heap allocations.
- Zero unsafe.
- Zero dependencies.
- `no_std`/WASM compatible.
- Fast.
- Stateless. All parsing methods are immutable.
- Simple and maintainable code (no magic numbers).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- The library must not panic. Any panic considered as a critical bug and should be reported.
- The library forbids unsafe code.
- No heap allocations, so crash due to OOM is not possible.
- All recursive methods have a depth limit.
- Technically, should use less than 64KiB of stack in worst case scenario.
- Most of arithmetic operations are checked.
- Most of numeric casts are checked.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- A font face.
- Parsed face tables.
- A 32-bit signed fixed-point number (16.16).
- A type-safe wrapper for glyph ID.
- A slice-like container that converts internal binary data only on access.
- A slice-like container that converts internal binary data only on access.
- An iterator over`LazyArray16`.
- An iterator over`LazyArray32`.
- A line metrics.
- A variation coordinate in a normalized coordinate system.
- A glyph’s raster image.
- A raw font face.
- A list of all supported tables as raw data.
- A rectangle.
- A rectangle described by the left-lower and upper-right points.
- A RGBA color in the sRGB color space.
- A script metrics used by subscript and superscript.
- A raw table record.
- A 4-byte tag.
- An affine transform.
- A font variation value.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- A list of errors that can occur during a CFF glyph outlining.
- A list of font face parsing errors.
- A glyph raster image format.
- A face style.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- A trait for parsing raw binary data of fixed size.
- A trait for glyph outline construction.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- Returns the number of fonts stored in a TrueType font collection.

# ttf_parser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ttf-parser/0.21.1/target-redirect/ttf_parser/

## Expand description

A high-level, safe, zero-allocation font parser for:

Font parsing starts with a [ Face](https://docs.rs/struct.Face.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- A high-level API for most common properties, hiding all parsing and data resolving logic.
- A low-level, but safe API to access TrueType tables data.
- Highly configurable. You can disable most of the features, reducing binary size. You can also parse TrueType tables separately, without loading the whole font/face.
- Zero heap allocations.
- Zero unsafe.
- Zero dependencies.
- `no_std`/WASM compatible.
- Fast.
- Stateless. All parsing methods are immutable.
- Simple and maintainable code (no magic numbers).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- The library must not panic. Any panic considered as a critical bug and should be reported.
- The library forbids unsafe code.
- No heap allocations, so crash due to OOM is not possible.
- All recursive methods have a depth limit.
- Technically, should use less than 64KiB of stack in worst case scenario.
- Most of arithmetic operations are checked.
- Most of numeric casts are checked.

# Face in ttf_parser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ttf-parser/^0.21/struct.Face.html

`pub struct Face<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A font face.

Provides a high-level API for working with TrueType fonts.
If you’re not familiar with how TrueType works internally, you should use this type.
If you do know and want a bit more low-level access - checkout [ FaceTables](https://docs.rs/struct.FaceTables.html).

Note that `Face` doesn’t own the font data and doesn’t allocate anything in heap.
Therefore you cannot “store” it. The idea is that you should parse the `Face`
when needed, get required data and forget about it.
That’s why the initial parsing is highly optimized and should not become a bottleneck.

If you still want to store `Face` - checkout
[owned_ttf_parser](https://crates.io/crates/owned_ttf_parser). Requires `unsafe`.

While `Face` is technically copyable, we disallow it because it’s almost 2KB big.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

`parse` insteadCreates a new [ Face](https://docs.rs/struct.Face.html) from a raw data.

`index` indicates the specific font face in a font collection.
Use [ fonts_in_collection](https://docs.rs/fn.fonts_in_collection.html) to get the total number of font faces.
Set to 0 if unsure.

This method will do some parsing and sanitization, but in general can be considered free. No significant performance overhead.

Required tables: `head`, `hhea` and `maxp`.

If an optional table has invalid data it will be skipped.

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#1752-1757)#### pub fn [is_outline_embedding_allowed](https://docs.rs#method.is_outline_embedding_allowed)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#1752-1757)

#### pub fn [is_outline_embedding_allowed](https://docs.rs#method.is_outline_embedding_allowed)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Checks if the face allows outline data to be embedded.

If false, only bitmaps may be embedded in accordance with [ Self::permissions](https://docs.rs/struct.Face.html#method.permissions).

If the font contains no bitmaps and this flag is not set, it implies no embedding is allowed.

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#1774-1776)#### pub fn [number_of_glyphs](https://docs.rs#method.number_of_glyphs)(&self) -> [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#1774-1776)

#### pub fn [number_of_glyphs](https://docs.rs#method.number_of_glyphs)(&self) -> [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)

Returns a total number of glyphs in the face.

Never zero.

The value was already parsed, so this function doesn’t involve any parsing.

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2044-2072)#### pub fn [outline_glyph](https://docs.rs#method.outline_glyph)(
    &self,
    glyph_id: [GlyphId](https://docs.rs/struct.GlyphId.html),
    builder: &mut dyn [OutlineBuilder](https://docs.rs/trait.OutlineBuilder.html)
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Rect](https://docs.rs/struct.Rect.html)>

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2044-2072)

#### pub fn [outline_glyph](https://docs.rs#method.outline_glyph)(
    &self,
    glyph_id: [GlyphId](https://docs.rs/struct.GlyphId.html),
    builder: &mut dyn [OutlineBuilder](https://docs.rs/trait.OutlineBuilder.html)
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Rect](https://docs.rs/struct.Rect.html)>

Outlines a glyph and returns its tight bounding box.

**Warning**: since `ttf-parser` is a pull parser,
`OutlineBuilder` will emit segments even when outline is partially malformed.
You must check `outline_glyph()` result before using
`OutlineBuilder`’s output.

`gvar`, `glyf`, `CFF` and `CFF2` tables are supported.
And they will be accesses in this specific order.

This method is affected by variation axes.

Returns `None` when glyph has no outline or on error.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use std::fmt::Write;
use ttf_parser;
struct Builder(String);
impl ttf_parser::OutlineBuilder for Builder {
    fn move_to(&mut self, x: f32, y: f32) {
        write!(&mut self.0, "M {} {} ", x, y).unwrap();
    }
    fn line_to(&mut self, x: f32, y: f32) {
        write!(&mut self.0, "L {} {} ", x, y).unwrap();
    }
    fn quad_to(&mut self, x1: f32, y1: f32, x: f32, y: f32) {
        write!(&mut self.0, "Q {} {} {} {} ", x1, y1, x, y).unwrap();
    }
    fn curve_to(&mut self, x1: f32, y1: f32, x2: f32, y2: f32, x: f32, y: f32) {
        write!(&mut self.0, "C {} {} {} {} {} {} ", x1, y1, x2, y2, x, y).unwrap();
    }
    fn close(&mut self) {
        write!(&mut self.0, "Z ").unwrap();
    }
}
let data = std::fs::read("tests/fonts/demo.ttf").unwrap();
let face = ttf_parser::Face::parse(&data, 0).unwrap();
let mut builder = Builder(String::new());
let bbox = face.outline_glyph(ttf_parser::GlyphId(1), &mut builder).unwrap();
assert_eq!(builder.0, "M 173 267 L 369 267 L 270 587 L 173 267 Z M 6 0 L 224 656 \
                       L 320 656 L 541 0 L 452 0 L 390 200 L 151 200 L 85 0 L 6 0 Z ");
assert_eq!(bbox, ttf_parser::Rect { x_min: 6, y_min: 0, x_max: 541, y_max: 656 });
```
[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2091-2093)#### pub fn [glyph_bounding_box](https://docs.rs#method.glyph_bounding_box)(&self, glyph_id: [GlyphId](https://docs.rs/struct.GlyphId.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Rect](https://docs.rs/struct.Rect.html)>

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2091-2093)

#### pub fn [glyph_bounding_box](https://docs.rs#method.glyph_bounding_box)(&self, glyph_id: [GlyphId](https://docs.rs/struct.GlyphId.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Rect](https://docs.rs/struct.Rect.html)>

Returns a tight glyph bounding box.

This is just a shorthand for `outline_glyph()` since only the `glyf` table stores
a bounding box. We ignore `glyf` table bboxes because they can be malformed.
In case of CFF and variable fonts we have to actually outline
a glyph to find it’s bounding box.

When a glyph is defined by a raster or a vector image,
that can be obtained via `glyph_image()`,
the bounding box must be calculated manually and this method will return `None`.

Note: the returned bbox is not validated in any way. A font file can have a glyph bbox set to zero/negative width and/or height and this is perfectly ok. For calculated bboxes, zero width and/or height is also perfectly fine.

This method is affected by variation axes.

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2097-2099)#### pub fn [global_bounding_box](https://docs.rs#method.global_bounding_box)(&self) -> [Rect](https://docs.rs/struct.Rect.html)

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2097-2099)

#### pub fn [global_bounding_box](https://docs.rs#method.global_bounding_box)(&self) -> [Rect](https://docs.rs/struct.Rect.html)

Returns a bounding box that large enough to enclose any glyph from the face.

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2122-2145)#### pub fn [glyph_raster_image](https://docs.rs#method.glyph_raster_image)(
    &self,
    glyph_id: [GlyphId](https://docs.rs/struct.GlyphId.html),
    pixels_per_em: [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[RasterGlyphImage](https://docs.rs/struct.RasterGlyphImage.html)<'_>>

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2122-2145)

#### pub fn [glyph_raster_image](https://docs.rs#method.glyph_raster_image)(
    &self,
    glyph_id: [GlyphId](https://docs.rs/struct.GlyphId.html),
    pixels_per_em: [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[RasterGlyphImage](https://docs.rs/struct.RasterGlyphImage.html)<'_>>

Returns a reference to a glyph’s raster image.

A font can define a glyph using a raster or a vector image instead of a simple outline. Which is primarily used for emojis. This method should be used to access raster images.

`pixels_per_em` allows selecting a preferred image size. The chosen size will
be closer to an upper one. So when font has 64px and 96px images and `pixels_per_em`
is set to 72, 96px image will be returned.
To get the largest image simply use `std::u16::MAX`.

Note that this method will return an encoded image. It should be decoded by the caller. We don’t validate or preprocess it in any way.

Also, a font can contain both: images and outlines. So when this method returns `None`
you should also try `outline_glyph()` afterwards.

There are multiple ways an image can be stored in a TrueType font
and this method supports most of them.
This includes `sbix`, `bloc` + `bdat`, `EBLC` + `EBDT`, `CBLC` + `CBDT`.
And font’s tables will be accesses in this specific order.

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2159-2161)#### pub fn [glyph_svg_image](https://docs.rs#method.glyph_svg_image)(&self, glyph_id: [GlyphId](https://docs.rs/struct.GlyphId.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[SvgDocument](https://docs.rs/svg/struct.SvgDocument.html)<'a>>

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2159-2161)

#### pub fn [glyph_svg_image](https://docs.rs#method.glyph_svg_image)(&self, glyph_id: [GlyphId](https://docs.rs/struct.GlyphId.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[SvgDocument](https://docs.rs/svg/struct.SvgDocument.html)<'a>>

Returns a reference to a glyph’s SVG image.

A font can define a glyph using a raster or a vector image instead of a simple outline. Which is primarily used for emojis. This method should be used to access SVG images.

Note that this method will return just an SVG data. It should be rendered or even decompressed (in case of SVGZ) by the caller. We don’t validate or preprocess it in any way.

Also, a font can contain both: images and outlines. So when this method returns `None`
you should also try `outline_glyph()` afterwards.

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2199-2214)

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2199-2214)

Paints a color glyph from the `COLR` table.

A font can have multiple palettes, which you can check via
[ color_palettes](https://docs.rs/struct.Face.html#method.color_palettes).
If unsure, just pass 0 to the

`palette` argument, which is the default.A font can define a glyph using layers of colored shapes instead of a
simple outline. Which is primarily used for emojis. This method should
be used to access glyphs defined in the `COLR` table.

Also, a font can contain both: a layered definition and outlines. So
when this method returns `None` you should also try
[ outline_glyph](https://docs.rs/struct.Face.html#method.outline_glyph) afterwards.

Returns `None` if the glyph has no `COLR` definition or if the glyph
definition is malformed.

See `examples/font2svg.rs` for usage examples.

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2219-2221)#### pub fn [variation_axes](https://docs.rs#method.variation_axes)(&self) -> [LazyArray16](https://docs.rs/struct.LazyArray16.html)<'a, [VariationAxis](https://docs.rs/fvar/struct.VariationAxis.html)>

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#2219-2221)

#### pub fn [variation_axes](https://docs.rs#method.variation_axes)(&self) -> [LazyArray16](https://docs.rs/struct.LazyArray16.html)<'a, [VariationAxis](https://docs.rs/fvar/struct.VariationAxis.html)>

Returns an iterator over variation axes.

Sets a variation axis coordinate.

This is one of the two only mutable methods in the library. We can simplify the API a lot by storing the variable coordinates in the face object itself.

Since coordinates are stored on the stack, we allow only 64 of them.

Returns `None` when face is not variable or doesn’t have such axis.

}## Expand description

Parsed face tables.

Unlike [ Face](https://docs.rs/struct.Face.html), provides a low-level parsing abstraction over TrueType tables.
Useful when you need a direct access to tables data.

Also, used when high-level API is problematic to implement. A good example would be OpenType layout tables (GPOS/GSUB).

# NormalizedCoordinate in ttf_parser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ttf-parser/^0.21/struct.NormalizedCoordinate.html

`pub struct NormalizedCoordinate(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

A variation coordinate in a normalized coordinate system.

Basically any number in a -1.0..1.0 range. Where 0 is a default value.

The number is stored as f2.16

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

A glyph’s raster image.

Note, that glyph metrics are in pixels and not in font units.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

# RawFace in ttf_parser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ttf-parser/^0.21/struct.RawFace.html

```
pub struct RawFace<'a> {
    pub data: &'a [
```
[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],
    pub table_records: [LazyArray16](https://docs.rs/struct.LazyArray16.html)<'a, [TableRecord](https://docs.rs/struct.TableRecord.html)>,
}## Expand description

A raw font face.

You are probably looking for [ Face](https://docs.rs/struct.Face.html). This is a low-level type.

Unlike [ Face](https://docs.rs/struct.Face.html),

[parses only face table records. Meaning all you can get from this type is a raw (](https://docs.rs/struct.RawFace.html)

`RawFace``&[u8]`) data of a requested table.
Then you can either parse just a singe table from a font/face or populate [manually before passing it to](https://docs.rs/struct.RawFaceTables.html)

`RawFaceTables`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Face.html#method.from_raw_tables)

`Face::from_raw_tables`## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.data)

`data: &'a [`[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)]The input font file data.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.table_records)

`table_records: `[LazyArray16](https://docs.rs/struct.LazyArray16.html)<'a, [TableRecord](https://docs.rs/struct.TableRecord.html)>An array of table records.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[source](https://docs.rs/src/ttf_parser/lib.rs.html#770-772)#### pub fn [from_slice](https://docs.rs#method.from_slice)(data: &'a [[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)], index: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [FaceParsingError](https://docs.rs/enum.FaceParsingError.html)>

`parse` instead

`index` indicates the specific font face in a font collection.

}## Expand description

A list of all supported tables as raw data.

This type should be used in tandem with
[ Face::from_raw_tables()](https://docs.rs/struct.Face.html#method.from_raw_tables).

This allows loading font faces not only from TrueType font files, but from any source. Mainly used for parsing WOFF.

# FaceParsingError in ttf_parser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ttf-parser/^0.21/enum.FaceParsingError.html

```
pub enum FaceParsingError {
    MalformedFont,
    UnknownMagic,
    FaceIndexOutOfBounds,
    NoHeadTable,
    NoHheaTable,
    NoMaxpTable,
}
```
## Expand description

A list of font face parsing errors.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MalformedFont)

### MalformedFont

An attempt to read out of bounds detected.

Should occur only on malformed fonts.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UnknownMagic)

### UnknownMagic

Face data must start with `0x00010000`, `0x74727565`, `0x4F54544F` or `0x74746366`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.FaceIndexOutOfBounds)

### FaceIndexOutOfBounds

The face index is larger than the number of faces in the font.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NoHeadTable)

### NoHeadTable

The `head` table is missing or malformed.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NoHheaTable)

### NoHheaTable

The `hhea` table is missing or malformed.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NoMaxpTable)

### NoMaxpTable

The `maxp` table is missing or malformed.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

# Permissions in ttf_parser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ttf-parser/^0.21/enum.Permissions.html

```
pub enum Permissions {
    Installable,
    Restricted,
    PreviewAndPrint,
    Editable,
}
```

# RasterImageFormat in ttf_parser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ttf-parser/^0.21/enum.RasterImageFormat.html

```
pub enum RasterImageFormat {
    PNG,
    BitmapMono,
    BitmapMonoPacked,
    BitmapGray2,
    BitmapGray2Packed,
    BitmapGray4,
    BitmapGray4Packed,
    BitmapGray8,
    BitmapPremulBgra32,
}
```
## Expand description

A glyph raster image format.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.PNG)

### PNG

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BitmapMono)

### BitmapMono

A monochrome bitmap.

The most significant bit of the first byte corresponds to the top-left pixel, proceeding through succeeding bits moving left to right. The data for each row is padded to a byte boundary, so the next row begins with the most significant bit of a new byte. 1 corresponds to black, and 0 to white.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BitmapMonoPacked)

### BitmapMonoPacked

A packed monochrome bitmap.

The most significant bit of the first byte corresponds to the top-left pixel, proceeding through succeeding bits moving left to right. Data is tightly packed with no padding. 1 corresponds to black, and 0 to white.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BitmapGray2)

### BitmapGray2

A grayscale bitmap with 2 bits per pixel.

The most significant bits of the first byte corresponds to the top-left pixel, proceeding through succeeding bits moving left to right. The data for each row is padded to a byte boundary, so the next row begins with the most significant bit of a new byte.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BitmapGray2Packed)

### BitmapGray2Packed

A packed grayscale bitmap with 2 bits per pixel.

The most significant bits of the first byte corresponds to the top-left pixel, proceeding through succeeding bits moving left to right. Data is tightly packed with no padding.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BitmapGray4)

### BitmapGray4

A grayscale bitmap with 4 bits per pixel.

The most significant bits of the first byte corresponds to the top-left pixel, proceeding through succeeding bits moving left to right. The data for each row is padded to a byte boundary, so the next row begins with the most significant bit of a new byte.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BitmapGray4Packed)

### BitmapGray4Packed

A packed grayscale bitmap with 4 bits per pixel.

The most significant bits of the first byte corresponds to the top-left pixel, proceeding through succeeding bits moving left to right. Data is tightly packed with no padding.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BitmapGray8)

### BitmapGray8

A grayscale bitmap with 8 bits per pixel.

The first byte corresponds to the top-left pixel, proceeding through succeeding bytes moving left to right.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BitmapPremulBgra32)

### BitmapPremulBgra32

A color bitmap with 32 bits per pixel.

The first group of four bytes corresponds to the top-left pixel, proceeding through
succeeding pixels moving left to right. Each byte corresponds to a color channel and the
channels within a pixel are in blue, green, red, alpha order. Color values are
pre-multiplied by the alpha. For example, the color “full-green with half translucency”
is encoded as `\x00\x80\x00\x80`, and not `\x00\xFF\x00\x80`.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

# fontdue - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fontdue/latest/target-redirect/fontdue/index.html

## Expand description

Fontdue is a font parser, rasterizer, and layout tool.

This is a no_std crate, but still requires the alloc crate.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [layout](https://docs.rs/layout/index.html)
- Tools for laying out strings of text.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Font](https://docs.rs/struct.Font.html)
- Represents a font. Fonts are immutable after creation and owns its own copy of the font data.
- [Font](https://docs.rs/struct.FontSettings.html)- Settings
- Settings for controlling specific font and layout behavior.
- [Line](https://docs.rs/struct.LineMetrics.html)- Metrics
- Metrics associated with line positioning.
- [Metrics](https://docs.rs/struct.Metrics.html)
- Encapsulates all layout information associated with a glyph for a fixed scale.
- [Outline](https://docs.rs/struct.OutlineBounds.html)- Bounds
- Defines the bounds for a glyph’s outline in subpixels. A glyph’s outline is always contained in its bitmap.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Font](https://docs.rs/type.FontResult.html)- Result
- Alias for Result<T, &’static str>.

---

# List of all items in this crate

# fontdue::layout - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fontdue/latest/target-redirect/fontdue/layout/index.html

## Expand description

Tools for laying out strings of text.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Character](https://docs.rs/struct.CharacterData.html)- Data
- Miscellaneous metadata associated with a character to assist in layout.
- [Glyph](https://docs.rs/struct.GlyphPosition.html)- Position
- A positioned scaled glyph.
- [Glyph](https://docs.rs/struct.GlyphRasterConfig.html)- Raster - Config
- Configuration for rasterizing a glyph. This struct is also a hashable key that can be used to uniquely identify a rasterized glyph for applications that want to cache glyphs.
- [Layout](https://docs.rs/struct.Layout.html)
- Text layout requires a small amount of heap usage which is contained in the Layout struct. This context is reused between layout calls. Reusing the Layout struct will greatly reduce memory allocations and is advisable for performance.
- [Layout](https://docs.rs/struct.LayoutSettings.html)- Settings
- Settings to configure how text layout is constrained. Text layout is considered best effort and layout may violate the constraints defined here if they prevent text from being laid out.
- [Line](https://docs.rs/struct.LinePosition.html)- Position
- Metrics about a positioned line.
- [Text](https://docs.rs/struct.TextStyle.html)- Style
- A style description for a segment of text.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Coordinate](https://docs.rs/enum.CoordinateSystem.html)- System
- The direction that the Y coordinate increases in. Layout needs to be aware of your coordinate system to place the glyphs correctly.
- [Horizontal](https://docs.rs/enum.HorizontalAlign.html)- Align
- Horizontal alignment options for text when a max_width is provided.
- [Vertical](https://docs.rs/enum.VerticalAlign.html)- Align
- Vertical alignment options for text when a max_height is provided.
- [Wrap](https://docs.rs/enum.WrapStyle.html)- Style
- Wrap style is a hint for how strings of text should be wrapped to the next line. Line wrapping can happen when the max width/height is reached.

---

# Font in fontdue - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fontdue/latest/target-redirect/fontdue/struct.Font.html

`pub struct Font { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Represents a font. Fonts are immutable after creation and owns its own copy of the font data.

This will perform the operation with the width multiplied by 3, as to simulate subpixels. Taking these as RGB values will perform subpixel anti aliasing.

# FontSettings in fontdue - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fontdue/latest/target-redirect/fontdue/struct.FontSettings.html

```
pub struct FontSettings {
    pub collection_index:
```
[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u32.html),
    pub scale: [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html),
    pub load_substitutions: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.bool.html),
}## Expand description

Settings for controlling specific font and layout behavior.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.collection_index)

`collection_index: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u32.html)The default is 0. The index of the font to use if parsing a font collection.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.scale)

`scale: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html)The default is 40. The scale in px the font geometry is optimized for. Fonts rendered at the scale defined here will be the most optimal in terms of looks and performance. Glyphs rendered smaller than this scale will look the same but perform slightly worse, while glyphs rendered larger than this will looks worse but perform slightly better. The units of the scale are pixels per Em unit.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.load_substitutions)

`load_substitutions: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.bool.html)The default is true. If enabled, will load glyphs for substitutions (liagtures, etc.) from
the gsub table on compatible fonts. Only makes a difference when using indexed operations,
i.e. `Font::raserize_indexed`, as singular characters do not have enough context to be
substituted.

# LineMetrics in fontdue - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fontdue/latest/target-redirect/fontdue/struct.LineMetrics.html

```
pub struct LineMetrics {
    pub ascent:
```
[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html),
    pub descent: [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html),
    pub line_gap: [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html),
    pub new_line_size: [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html),
}## Expand description

Metrics associated with line positioning.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.ascent)

`ascent: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html)The highest point that any glyph in the font extends to above the baseline. Typically positive.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.descent)

`descent: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html)The lowest point that any glyph in the font extends to below the baseline. Typically negative.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.line_gap)

`line_gap: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html)The gap to leave between the descent of one line and the ascent of the next. This is of course only a guideline given by the font’s designers.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.new_line_size)

`new_line_size: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html)A precalculated value for the height or width of the line depending on if the font is laid out horizontally or vertically. It’s calculated by: ascent - descent + line_gap.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

# Metrics in fontdue - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fontdue/latest/target-redirect/fontdue/struct.Metrics.html

```
pub struct Metrics {
    pub xmin:
```
[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.i32.html),
    pub ymin: [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.i32.html),
    pub width: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html),
    pub height: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html),
    pub advance_width: [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html),
    pub advance_height: [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html),
    pub bounds: [OutlineBounds](https://docs.rs/struct.OutlineBounds.html),
}## Expand description

Encapsulates all layout information associated with a glyph for a fixed scale.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.xmin)

`xmin: `[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.i32.html)Whole pixel offset of the left-most edge of the bitmap. This may be negative to reflect the glyph is positioned to the left of the origin.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.ymin)

`ymin: `[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.i32.html)Whole pixel offset of the bottom-most edge of the bitmap. This may be negative to reflect the glyph is positioned below the baseline.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.width)

`width: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html)The width of the bitmap in whole pixels.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.height)

`height: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html)The height of the bitmap in whole pixels.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.advance_width)

`advance_width: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html)Advance width of the glyph in subpixels. Used in horizontal fonts.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.advance_height)

`advance_height: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html)Advance height of the glyph in subpixels. Used in vertical fonts.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.bounds)

`bounds: `[OutlineBounds](https://docs.rs/struct.OutlineBounds.html)The bounding box that contains the glyph’s outline at the offsets specified by the font. This is always a smaller box than the bitmap bounds.

# OutlineBounds in fontdue - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fontdue/latest/target-redirect/fontdue/struct.OutlineBounds.html

## Expand description

Defines the bounds for a glyph’s outline in subpixels. A glyph’s outline is always contained in its bitmap.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.xmin)

`xmin: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html)Subpixel offset of the left-most edge of the glyph’s outline.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.ymin)

`ymin: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html)Subpixel offset of the bottom-most edge of the glyph’s outline.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.width)

`width: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html)The width of the outline in subpixels.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.height)

`height: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.f32.html)The height of the outline in subpixels.
